Clone selection

Next steps for A01, A07, A12, A03, A06, A10

  1. Validate: sequence each clone in both directions and read every designed change; a second PCR with primers outside the first pair excludes allelic dropout and a large deletion on one allele. Where a clone carries different silent changes on its two alleles, confirm which allele carries which (clone the amplicon or sequence it deeply). Check the predicted off-target sites of the guides.
  2. Karyotype: SNP array of the clones carried forward and the parental line (copy number, loss of heterozygosity at the edited locus, recurrent gains).
  3. Bank: expand the first-choice clones and freeze several vials of each at low passage from the validated pool; keep one reserve vial of the clone held back.
  4. Quality control: mycoplasma, identity (STR) against the parental line, pluripotency markers, and whole-genome sequencing of the final two or three clones.

Suggested steps; adapt them to your own workflow.

All clones aligned

Best clone first. Every clone is laid onto the same stretch of the wild-type control read, base by base. Guides (grey bar, PAM darker), cuts and designed changes are marked. A base that differs from the control is highlighted; a dash is a base the clone lacks.

Method and limits

  • Each edited trace is compared with its control. Over a window around the cut(s), the mix of bases at every position is fitted as a non-negative mixture of the alleles expected from the design (wild type, indels at each cut, deletions between cuts, the donor's complete edit, and partial conversions).
  • Intervals are 95% intervals: the profile of the fit (what the trace cannot tell apart) widened by a margin calibrated on simulated traces built from real controls; they have not yet been calibrated on laboratory mixtures. The confidence tier is the width of the interval, not the number of warnings.
  • Detection limit is about 5% per allele; abundances are trace-derived estimates, not allele counts. Deletions or insertions larger than the readable window, large deletions on one allele, loss of heterozygosity and copy-number changes are not visible.
  • A clone call assumes at most two alleles. Sanger traces cannot tell a homozygous clone from one with a large deletion on the other allele.
  • Junction reads show whether the knock-in sequence is correct and reaches genomic sequence beyond the homology arm; they cannot show zygosity or copy number.
  • Genome-wide off-target editing is not assessed.
